## The problem

Our engineering team of twelve has drifted into long-lived feature branches that often survive for two or three weeks before merging. Every merge now feels like an event rather than a routine: last month's payments refactor required four separate rebases before it could land cleanly, and the person doing the merging spent most of a day untangling conflicts that had nothing to do with their own work. Because integration happens so late, bugs surface only after branches converge, at which point it is often unclear whether a regression came from one feature or another. Code review suffers too — reviewers face sprawling diffs that are hard to reason about carefully, so review quality drops exactly when the stakes are highest. The underlying incentive is backwards: engineers are effectively rewarded for polishing a branch in isolation rather than for integrating small, verified changes continuously.

## The proposal

I propose we move to trunk-based development, where everyone commits small, frequent changes directly to main behind feature flags. Concretely, this means:

- Branches live no longer than one to two days before merging
- New or risky code ships behind feature flags rather than on separate branches
- CI must pass on every commit to main, with no exceptions
- Pull requests are capped at a size reviewers can meaningfully evaluate in under 30 minutes
- We hold a two-week pilot with one team before rolling out company-wide

This should shrink merge pain, surface bugs while context is still fresh, and make review meaningfully better.

## What could go wrong

The strongest objection is that trunk-based development demands real discipline around feature flags and test coverage — without both, we risk shipping half-finished work to main and destabilizing production more often, not less. That risk is legitimate: teams with weak flag hygiene or thin CI have been burned by this transition. I don't think we can dismiss it; instead, the pilot should specifically test whether we can build that discipline before we commit further.

I would like a decision by the end of next week.
